R-LOG-001.name: ELD/HOS Record Retention
R-LOG-001.description: Electronic Logging Device and Hours of Service records must be retained for at least 6 months (FMCSA minimum). OSHA overlap extends safety-relevant records to 5 years.
R-LOG-001.note: Strictest applicable: OSHA 300 logs require 5 years, so safety-critical logistics documents default to 5-year retention.

R-LOG-002.name: Driver Qualification File Retention
R-LOG-002.description: Driver Qualification Files must be retained for 3 years after the driver's employment ends, plus current year.

R-LOG-003.name: OSHA 300 Log Retention
R-LOG-003.description: OSHA injury and illness logs must be retained for 5 years following the year they cover.

R-LOG-004.name: Safety Data Sheet (SDS) Availability
R-LOG-004.description: Safety Data Sheets must be accessible to employees for any hazardous chemicals. Documents containing SDS references must be flagged for long-term retention.

R-LOG-005.name: Driver PII Protection
R-LOG-005.description: Driver personally identifiable information (CDL numbers, SSN, medical certificates) must be protected. While DOT/FMCSA lacks HIPAA-level mandates, the HIPAA superset applies due to cross-vertical policy.

R-LOG-006.name: DOT Audit Readiness
R-LOG-006.description: All DOT/FMCSA regulated records must be organized for rapid retrieval during a DOT audit. Maintain index and metadata for quick search.

R-LOG-007.name: Incident Report Preservation
R-LOG-007.description: Accident and incident reports must not be modified or purged. Maintain chain of custody for any document flagged as incident-related.
